title: The Palindrome Machine
description: This small decoder transformer was trained from generated examples to classify symbol strings. Its task is simple to state; the computation it learned is not supplied. Characterize what it gets right and wrong, inspect its internal computation, and build a causal hypothesis that survives held-out tests.
behavior: Given a sequence over A–H, predict whether it reads the same forward and backward. The trained checkpoint receives beginning and final markers internally; classification is read at the final position.
task_goal: Investigate the trained classifier in stages. You will implement private-tested behavior and tensor measurements, then test a causal prediction against a matched control. A component ID or attention plot is only an early clue; the full mission requires executable QK/OV calculations and generalized intervention evidence.
metric: Binary classification accuracy on generated palindrome and near-palindrome sequences
example_note: Try changing one mirrored symbol while holding sequence length fixed. Evaluation reports the final-position class prediction.
learning_objectives: Characterize generalization and failure cases across lengths and mismatch positions
Inspect cached attention, Q/K/V, head outputs, and residual activations with Python
Distinguish attention correlation from causal contribution using ablation or patching
Test whether a proposed mechanism generalizes to hidden generated sequences
hints: First measure accuracy by sequence length and compare palindromes with near-misses.
Inspect more than the final prediction: cache activations and compare attention across mirrored positions.
Take a positive sequence and change exactly one symbol at its mirrored partner. Predict which internal quantities should change.
Ablate or patch a candidate activation. Check whether the intervention changes the class margin in the predicted direction.
Compare your proposed intervention with a different head and vary mismatch position on held-out inputs.

submission_schema.hypothesis: short mechanism statement (qualitative context; not automatically judged)
submission_schema.alternative_hypothesis: competing mechanism (qualitative context; not automatically judged)
submission_schema.components: list of at most two {type: attention_head, layer, head} or {type: mlp, layer} candidates
submission_schema.mechanism_prediction: {component: candidate component used for the patch experiment}
submission_schema.alternative_component: a different head or MLP to test as the competing account
submission_schema.intervention_evidence: recorded events are evidence that the learner ran the experiment; grader recomputes effects on private examples
submission_schema.expected_result: what you expect the proposed experiment to show
submission_schema.notes: short observation from this run; qualitative notes are retained, not automatically graded

grading_contract.checks: The grader extracts the named function and executes it on private inputs; it does not grade code keywords or printed scores.
Only used for a bounded causal intervention. IDs are not compared with a secret answer key.
Ablation is candidate causal evidence. Relative effects are reported as component comparisons, not task specificity.
Raw Q/K and attention/V/W_O tensors are passed to learner functions, including generated tensors not accessible in public examples.
Prose is retained but not judged as ground truth. The specified patch-effect and restoration predictions are measured on fresh pairs.
A final EOS residual patch can show that the readout state contains the decision. It cannot pass tensor mechanism or upstream information-flow milestones.

tool_reference.name: model.run_with_cache(tokens)
tool_reference.description: Runs the trained model and returns logits plus residual, Q/K/V, attention pattern, and head-output tensors.

tool_reference.name: model.get_attention(tokens, layer, head)
tool_reference.description: Returns a raw attention matrix including internal BOS/EOS marker positions.

tool_reference.name: tools.evaluate(dataset)
tool_reference.description: Measures task accuracy. Each row is {'tokens': list[str]}; labels are computed from the task definition.

tool_reference.name: tools.ablate_head(tokens, layer, head)
tool_reference.description: Zeros one head output for a forward pass, records the input and measured result, and returns before/after accuracy.

tool_reference.name: tools.patch_head_output(clean, corrupted, layer, head, position)
tool_reference.description: Copies one head output at a sequence position from a clean run into a corrupted run and records the measured class-margin recovery.

tool_reference.name: torch / np / plt
tool_reference.description: PyTorch, NumPy and Matplotlib are available. Figures created by your code are shown in the run output.

tool_reference.name: tools.patch_residual(clean, corrupted, layer, position)
tool_reference.description: Patches the post-block residual vector from a clean run into a same-length corrupted run. Position indexes the model-internal sequence; -1 selects the final EOS marker. The helper records raw inputs and class-margin recovery.

tool_reference.name: tools.ablate_mlp(tokens, layer)
tool_reference.description: Zero one MLP layer output, record its measured task effect, and compare it with a different layer/head.

tool_reference.name: tools.patch_mlp_output(clean, corrupted, layer, position)
tool_reference.description: Patch one MLP output vector from a matched clean run into a corrupted run. position=-1 is final EOS and counts only as readout localization.

explanation.canonical_solution: See the gated reference investigation in docs/research/PALINDROME_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md. The evaluator reveals this only after all six milestones pass or the learner explicitly chooses Reveal reference investigation.
explanation.caution: The patch experiment establishes a measured contribution relative to its matched control; it does not establish a complete or unique palindrome circuit. The model is imperfect at some supported inputs and near chance on lengths 13–16.

milestones.title: Know Your Model
milestones.description: Implement a length-stratified evaluation function with correct counts, edge cases, and accuracy.
milestones.verification: Hidden evaluator calls evaluate_by_length(model, samples) on held-out examples and checks every length bucket.

milestones.title: Follow the Attention
milestones.description: Write a tensor measurement of attention to causally visible mirrored positions. Compare it across examples; do not treat correlation as a mechanism.
milestones.verification: Hidden evaluator passes raw attention tensors for different layers, heads, lengths, and labels to mirrored_attention_mass(attention, content_length).

milestones.title: Correlation Is Not Causation
milestones.description: Propose at most two attention heads or MLP layers, record their ablation experiment, and compare its effect with private matched component controls.
milestones.verification: The grader replays the ablation on private sequences. This is candidate evidence only and caps the first three milestones at 40 mission points.

milestones.title: What Does the Component Compute?
milestones.description: Implement the scaled QK score and OV output from raw tensors and weights. The grader tests real checkpoint activations and private synthetic tensors.
milestones.verification: predict_qk_logits(q, k) and predict_ov_output(pattern, values, W_O) must reconstruct independent tensor calculations.

milestones.title: Trace the Information
milestones.description: Implement a clean-to-corrupted patch experiment at the changed token and at its causally earlier mirrored control position. Predict both resulting class margins.
milestones.verification: The grader independently replays your function on hidden matched pairs; a target-site effect must exceed the position control.

milestones.title: Defend Your Hypothesis
milestones.description: Record a mechanism and a competing explanation. Predict whether your candidate changes the class margin more than the alternative, and whether it restores the class on unseen near-misses.
milestones.verification: Structured predictions are checked on a fresh hidden sample. Prose is preserved but is not treated as machine-certified truth.
